                                                        MEETING SYNOPSIS


                 INCLINE VILLAGE GENERAL IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT BOARD OF TRUSTEES
                            HELD IN INCLINE VILLAGE ON WEDNESDAY, September 9, 2026


  *Viewing available by clicking the link and choosing BOT Meeting 09.09.2026 at: https://ivgid.portal.civicclerk.com/event/745/media




This summary outlines what actions the Board took, along with major discussions and updates
important to the Incline Village/Crystal Bay community.

The IVGID Board of Trustees began at 4:00 PM.

    •    All Trustees were present: Chair Michaela Tonking, Vice Chair Michelle Jezycki, Trustees Mick
         Homan, Dave Noble, and Ray Tulloch.
    •    Trustee candidates present: Ryan Brooks and Dave Noble.
    •    Public comment held.

Initial Public Comments – Key Topics Raised (No Board Action) Community members spoke about:

    •    Need for senior-friendly recreation programs and senior transportation.
    •    Concerns about property tax increases and fee equity.
    •    Opinions on recreation and beach fees.
    •    Feedback on staff behavior concerns and board responses to public.
    •    Praise for Chateau event staff.
    •    Concern about beach access fairness for local families.
    •    Ongoing issues with tree vandalism.
    •    Requests to ensure respectful treatment of IVGID staff at events and facilities.

Approval of Agenda
  • One change: Item H3 (Dell purchase order) moved from consent to general business as Item I1.
  • Agenda approved.

Board of Trustees – Item F Updates

    •    Chair Michaela Tonking – Senior Transportation Update
         Chair Tonking reported attending a meeting with community representatives and the Washoe
         County Senior Services Program to explore options for reestablishing senior transportation.
         Discussions emphasized the original scope of the former program and reviewed current needs
         based on collected data. Washoe County is beginning budget development for potential services
         comparable to those offered in Gerlach and other outlying areas. Progress is slow but moving
         forward. Chair Tonking and District Manager Bob Harrison will continue coordination with the
         County Manager.

    •    Trustee & Board Treasurer Mick Homan – Financial Compliance, Fiscal Watch, and
         Misinformation
            o State Compliance & Fiscal Watch:
                He reported on a meeting with the Nevada Committee on Local Government Finance
                (CLGF), which oversees IVGID during fiscal watch. IVGID is now fully compliant with all
                reporting requirements. The Fiscal Year 2026 audit is underway and ahead of schedule.
                The CLGF and Department of Taxation praised staff for rapid progress and reconfirmed
                plans to remove IVGID from fiscal watch this fall upon audit completion.
            o Addressing Misinformation:
                Trustee Homan outlined recent instances of community misinformation, including
                inaccurate claims presented at the CLGF meeting and the IVCBA community forum. He
                clarified that accounting control issues have been resolved, the 2025 audit was fully
                clean, and the district posted significant surpluses across funds in 2025 and positive
                momentum in 2026. He refuted claims of a nonexistent $5 million loss and addressed
                misinformation about beach access policies, facility fees, and the beach house project.
                Trustee Homan emphasized that the beach house aligns with community survey
                priorities, is compliant with TRPA constraints, and includes significant facility
                improvements. He urged residents to rely on official IVGID communications and directly
                contact staff or trustees with questions.

    •    Vice Chair Michelle Jezycki – Community Engagement, Staff Safety, Beach House
         Progress, and Misinformation
            o Chateau Open House:
               She praised strong community engagement and staff efforts during the districtwide open
               house event.

o     Conduct at Public Events:
                    Vice Chair Jezycki expressed concern about a recent hostile incident toward staff and
                    community members, emphasizing that aggression at IVGID meetings or events is
                    unacceptable and should result in appropriate consequences.
              o     Beach House Construction:
                    She thanked Public Works and noted rapid visible progress on the new beach house,
                    confirming that the project remains both on time and on budget.
              o     Combating Misinformation:
                    Echoing Trustee Homan, she warned that intentional misinformation—by candidates or
                    residents—causes harm in a small community. She encouraged residents to attend
                    meetings, ask questions, email trustees, and share verified information.
              o     Tree Vandalism Investigation:
                    Vice Chair Jezycki expressed frustration with slow progress in responding to leads
                    regarding recent tree vandalism but expects updates soon, acknowledging sheriff’s
                    resource constraints during evacuations.
              o     Senior Transportation Coordination:
                    She reaffirmed IVGID’s partnership role with Washoe County, noting ongoing challenges
                    and the importance of finding workable solutions.

         No formal actions taken.

General Manager and Staff Reports (Information Only) The GM and department leaders reported:

    •    Emergency power outage response evaluations and plans to improve backup systems.
    •    Sheriff’s investigation into tree poisoning; reward program being launched with public press
         conference.
    •    Successful community open house held.
    •    Recreation venue usage and financial trends discussed.
    •    IT updates and progress on Tyler financial system implementation.
    •    Finance reported strong audit progress, investment strategies, and capital planning progress.
    •    Public Works gave major construction updates, including:
             o Effluent Pipeline Project completed early and under budget.
             o Skate Park Enhancement Project is completed.
             o Rec Center HVAC upgrades underway.
             o Incline Beach House Project is continuing on schedule.

No Board actions were taken under reports.

Tahoe Meadows – Feasibility Study Presentation (No Board Action Yet) Nevada Tahoe
Conservation District presented a study on potential off-highway parking/bathroom facilities near Tahoe
Meadows, referencing the IVGID-owned 5-acre parcel.
